beats.headline: On Louis's lap
beats.text: I am on Louis's lap, because Louis is sweet. Now the other crawlers in the quadrant have found Carl's group, and Carl's group has a cat who talks. Their manager, Mordecai, is sobering Louis and Firas up on the spot. All the fun is coming out of their blood at once. Louis looks very sad about it. I am not sad. I am here, and I am staying.

beats.headline: A room that is not a way home
beats.text: The Toe is full of children, forty of them, and I am handing out juice boxes. Carl takes everybody into his room. The kids knock over the couch, grab the robot, and make a gambling ring out of the straws. I turn into a hairy monster and the robot gets dropped. Then the eagle puts a movie on the screen and it goes quiet. I ask Carl if the room can take us home. It cannot. There was a way, and it went with the town hall. Stop the gnomes, and my people live, and I will tell him what we seek.

beats.headline: Two in the rock man
beats.text: I touch the rock man, and he's hot, and there are two in there. So I tell Carl to bring these two guys. He doesn't get it. I grab his hand and pull. He doesn't get that either. Katia shoots the rock man, and I tell Carl straight: that's your friend Chris, don't kill him. There's also an Infiltrator in there. Kill that one. Carl asks can I turn into one of those worms and go in after her. No. They're too small. And that's a pretty messed-up thing to ask.

beats.headline: I lied about the Gate
beats.text: Henrik is my brother. He's a Principal. People say they're a cult that catalogues every known species. They're looking for one, and it's Quetzalcoatlus. I told Carl the Gate of the Feral Gods was a myth. I lied. It's real, and it's dangerous. It opens a way from one place to the next, and when it closes, an ancient feral god comes through on the side that opened it. We could go home, and this world would pay for it. That's why even my brother doesn't want to use it. He's not that cruel.

beats.headline: My brother pushed too hard
beats.text: Carl has been sitting there tense and angry for minutes, and he is scaring the children, so I tell him. He says it is weird being the one who has to wait. He crashed a drop bear into a god's face. He says that was hours ago. He reminds me of my brother. Always moving, always pushing at his goal. When something got in front of him that he could not figure out, he pushed too hard. If he had waited, he would still be alive.

beats.headline: Waiting on the last stage
beats.text: Carl and Donut and me, and the dromedarians rebuilding a town that will not exist in a few hours. Carl explains the last stage out loud, cheerfully, to anybody listening: open a portal to the ninth floor, keep the second watch, and send me through with the rest. I made him promise about my people. I am holding him to it.

beats.headline: We are going to be married
beats.text: The watch Chris threw is not my brother's watch. It is a fake. Carl has changed the plan: no god, they are keeping the gate, and I am to fly for the water, go through to Larracos, stay hidden and tell the others what they really are. Watch over my people, I tell him. We have a deal. And keep Louis safe. I love him. We are going to be married. Carl asks if I am serious. I am. I become a skyfowl and go.

beats.headline: Wearing the elf's mother
beats.text: The viceroy's head comes off and rolls across the table. I push the body aside, sit in his chair, twirl his mask and put my feet up. Hello again, boys. I'm wearing Epitome Noflex, the bald elf's mother, and he screams that his men told him I was dead. Obviously not. Faceless regenerates at sunset anyway. He wants the fish to intervene. The fish says I'm an NPC, not on Carl's team, the AI won't touch it, and they're free to kill me. Gotta catch me first. Then Carl looks right at me. Hello, Juice Box.

beats.headline: My people, their own team
beats.text: Donut says hi. I ask how Louis is. Sad, she says, because Firas died. Poor kid. Then business. I know what I am now, and I know what they are. If they want me to stop knocking down their pretty structures, they make a rule: my people seated as a team of their own, with the same safeties, regeneration for all of us. Baldie says it's not going to happen. Carl files it anyway, and I add full voting rights. Then I click a hobgoblin pus detonator. Ten seconds. Vote no, and this keeps happening. Tell Louis I send my love. I leave as a bat.

beats.headline: Through the portal with the water
beats.text: I went through the Gate with the water. I lay low with the ones who lived through it, and when they were ready I told them. What they are. What this whole place is. Enough of them believed me that they call me Warlord now, and a Warlord has people, and a Warlord has opinions about alliances. I have sent War Leader Arief to Carl's people with my terms. The terms are Louis. He marries me. That is the alliance.

beats.headline: Not what I wanted
beats.text: Carl. You didn't do what I wanted. We wanted everybody protected, with regeneration. He says they would never allow it, so they did the next best thing: they made it so we can kill them. It'll have to do. I show him most of my papers. Some go in the drawer. I ask about Ruby. The rules of this world are a lot. A voice told me I would not be allowed to talk to someone I tried to meet. I don't have menus. I do have messaging, so now Louis and I can talk whenever we like.

beats.headline: Burned some assets
beats.text: Carl sends me a message for Ferdinand. I pass it on. I had to burn some assets to save his ass. I hope it was worth it. I'm hearing about strange movements, and I relay all of it to Louis and Britney. Heads up to his people. We are powering up the towers early. Anyone in town who is not in his army should start moving into his territory.

beats.headline: A single statement
beats.text: Odette presses me, and I have a single statement. Fuck all of you. You had no right to do what you did to my people. You bicker and you murder and you cannot even take care of yourselves, and your real world is in shambles, and you play gods with people like me: implant memories, give our children imaginary diseases, give us dreams that do not exist, and take it all away for your own amusement. Then I change my shape, and I tell everyone watching that it is coming for them all. I walk out through the wall.

beats.headline: The skyfowl works it out
beats.text: The skyfowl says it is all about the gods. That we are risking everything to touch as many as we can. I don't answer that. I tell him we lost three in Club Vanquisher. We didn't let the gods out; we were in position just in case. One of us touched Bast, the panther god, but she died before she could escape. Only one of us has touched a deity, and that one is wrong. Three of us touched the basilica ogres. He says he can show us how to touch a god and not get killed. The digger under his feet moves away.

beats.headline: Where is my husband
beats.text: Carl comes running across the courtyard shouting about generators and railings and waffle makers. I turn human and grab his shoulder. Where is Louis? Where is my husband? He is not answering me. Carl says he is alive but in trouble, and someone is trying to rescue him, and it is Samantha. So I tell Samantha. I have a form that is a fleshmancer. Bring my husband back in one piece and she can have any body she wants. I know who she really is.

beats.headline: A hunter wraith
beats.text: The halls in here move. The system knows where you're headed and makes one passage there for you. We got inside this castle a few times. We lost the asset who knew it best. We're not headed for the throne room. Not yet. I change into a hunter wraith. Where is he? Carl finds my husband on the map, in a line of cubicles, a room no bigger than a coffin, with Samantha on the other side of the wall. Got it. I'll tell him when I have Louis. I go invisible.

beats.headline: The Inevitable Ruin
beats.text: I put Louis on the cot and kiss his forehead. Carl says it seems strange that I love him. The first time, he had me become a Dewi, who looks into the hearts of men. He is genuine. He clings to every drop of happiness. He was my anchor. Then I possessed him as a hunter wraith, and its curse, the Inevitable Ruin, showed me the truth. He is terrified of me. He thinks NPCs fall for him because of some ability. He will never trust what I feel. Hopeless? Not even close, cowboy. Wait until you see what Justice Light has cooked up.

beats.headline: The long way round
beats.text: Louis comes out of the tent holding his throat. I say something to him and he says something back, and I put my hands to my face and turn away. Then, in chat: I will be leaving about ten seconds after everyone else. Carl wants to know where. Oh, I'm going to the twelfth floor all right. Justice Light and I are taking the long way. It's okay, Carl. Trust me. You'll like this one.
